Mr. Dr. Shahdeen Malik, Advocate with Mr. Z. I. Khan Panna, Advocate (in person) ------for the Petitioner.

parties:
Z.I. Khan Panna
Vs.
Govt. Of Bangladesh and Others
full_judgment:
Farah Mahbub, J: In this Rule, issued under Article 102 of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh, the respondents have been called upon to show cause as to why the recruitment process so initiated pursuant to the advertisement for recruitment of Inspector of Food (at serial No. 1), Sub-Inspector of Food (serial No. 2) and Assistant Sub- Inspector of Food (serial No. 7) so published in the "Daily Star" on 21.09.2010 (Annexure-B) should not be declared to be without lawful authority and is of no legal effect for having changed the marking system at the stage of viva voce examination. 

 4. It has been stated that the Directorate of Food under the Ministry of Food vide Memo No. প্রশা/সংস্থা/১/ নিয়োগ-০৯/২০১০-১১০৮ dated 16.9.2010, had decided to recruit employees against 10(ten) categories of posts including those of Inspector of Food, Sub- Inspector of Food, Supervisor, Auditor, Upper Division Clerk, Accountant-cum-Cashier, Office Assistant-cum-Computer Composer, Data Entry/Control Operator, and Assistant Operator, in total 1552 posts(Annexure-A). The said decision was duly published in the "Daily Star", a national newspaper, on 21.9.2010 as an advertisement for recruitment (Annexure-B). In response thereof the aspirant candidates filed applications for appointment in the respective posts. Ultimately, the recruitment process of written and viva-voce examinations had been duly completed for the posts of Supervisor(13 posts), Auditor(16 posts), Upper Division Clerk(51 posts), Accountant-cum-Cashier(15 posts), Data Entry/Control Operator(5 posts) and Assistant Operator(41 posts). However, appointment letters for none of those posts have yet been issued by the said Directorate. 

 5. It has also been contended that the number of vacant posts for Food Inspector are 328(at serial No.1), for Food Sub-Inspector 175 and the number of Assistant Sub-Inspector are 405 (at serial No. 7). It has been stated that the written examination for the post of Inspector of Food and Sub-Inspector of Food were held on 23.12.2011 and that for recruitment of Assistant Sub-Inspector of Food was held on 25.05.2012. The result of both the written examinations were published on 11.1.2012. 

 11. It this regard it has been asserted that a total 10 (ten) categories of posts were advertised for recruitment on 21.09.2010 including these 3(three) posts of Inspector of Food, Sub-Inspector of Food and Assistant Sub-Inspector of Food (Annexure 13). However, the written and viva race examination of the candidates for the other 6(six) categories of posts had been calculated in accordance with the earlier criterion i.e., 80% for written and 20% for viva-voce examination and that the examination process for those posts had already been completed. Per contra, when the recruitment process of the remaining 3(three) posts was still pending the marking distribution had been charged vide Memo dated 5.5.2013 causing grave prejudice to the interest of the candidates for those 3(three) categories of posts. Moreso, the said changed marking criterion is prone to arbitrariness and mass corruption, as has also been reported in a number of national daily newspapers. (Annexure-I and J respectively); whereas, clause (da) as contained in Memo No. প্রশা/সংস্থা/১/নিয়োগ-০৯/২০১০-১১০৮ dated 16.09.2010 which was published in the "Daily Star" on 21.09.2010 (Annexure B) the Directorate of Food, categorically states , inter-alia, 

 14. Further, it has been stated that the actual figure of candidates was not fixed in 90 for taking viva voce examination, as claimed by the petitioner, for in different dates the number of candidates was below 90 and a good number of candidates were absent during the course of interview; hence, it was not correct that everyday viva voce examination was conducted by the respective . Selection Committees for 450 candidates. In this connection it has been emphatically asserted that the appointment process involves a number of actions which the appointing authority needs to complete gradually. Since the number of candidates were near about 4(four) lacs hence, to conduct written examination making accommodation was a big difficulty; it also took time to get budgetary allocation from the Ministry of Finance as it involved handsome amount of money; besides, there was shortage of manpower to conduct such a big examination by the appointing authority; also, it required sufficient time to scrutinize applications, to enter the data into the system, to conduct examination and to publish results etc. Moreover, the written examination so held on 27.01.2012 for the post of Assistant Sub-Inspector had to be suspended on 02.02.2012 due to the allegation of leak out of question paper prior to the examination. Later, the authority made new arrangement to conduct the said examination afresh, which was ultimately held on 25.05.2012. Above all, as the advertisement for appointment was made for 10(ten) categories of posts the results were also needed to be published for those posts all together. However, due to above unavoidable contingencies it took time to complete the whole recruitment process (Annexure-7). 

 17. Mr. Dr. Shahdeen Malik, the Warned Advocate appearing with Mr. Z. I. Khan Panna, the learned Advocate (in person) for the petitioner submits that the advertisement for those 3(three) impugned posts were published on 21.09.2010 e.g., exactly 3(three) years ago, but unfortunately the recruitment process has not yet been completed long after 3(three) years; thus, clearly indicates that the process of recruitment is not bonafide but a malafide one. He further submits that the sudden rush to complete the process of  viva-voce examination within 7-8 working days by forming 5(five) separate Selection Committees at the fag end of the central government indicates a mala fide intention of recruiting a particular type of candidates, not based on merit and qualifications. He also goes to argue that the condition as enumerated in clause (da) of the advertisement dated 21.09.2010 to the effect that the recruitment would the entirely based on merit and qualifications and any improper request or personal solicitation for the sake of securing employment in any of those posts would render the candidate disqualified, had clearly not been followed in the instant case and as such, the recruitment process is mala fide and arbitrary. Again, he goes to contend that whimsical change in the composition of the Selection Committee to 5(five) different Selection Committees for recruitment which were to sit in Divisional headquarters, to conduct the viva-voce examinations, clearly indicates that these Selection Committees were formed with ulterior purpose and goal to recruit on the basis of improper request and solicitation. He also submits that each Selection Committee is tasked with conducting viva-voce examinations of 90 candidates each day and a total 450 candidates are to be interviewed each day thus, clearly goes to show- that the whole process of the so called viva-voce examination is a sham and not a proper and bona fide examination for assessment and selection of the most suitable candidates in terms of merit and qualification. He again goes to argue that the viva-voce examination for some of the posts carried a weightage of 20% while the viva-voce for the rest i.e. more than one thousand posts now carry the weightage of 30% marks; such change in the marks for written and viva-voce examination pending recruitment process is improper, illegal and is not tenable in the eye of law and as such the resultant recruitment process is without lawful authority and hence, is of no legal effect. He lastly submits that due to publication of news reports and launching of investigation Mere is an over-riding perception  that the impugned recruitment process for appointment of Inspector of Food, Sub-Inspector of Food and Assistant Sub-Inspector of Food is vitiated by external considerations and when recruitment is not based on merit and qualification this Hon'ble Court must interfere to prevent souls biased and motivated executive action for the cause of justice, equity and fair play. 

 18. Mr. Mahbubey Alam, the learned Attorney General with Ms. Amatul Karim, the learned Deputy. Attorney General with Ms. Nusrat Jahan, the learned Assistant Attorney General appearing on behalf of respondent-government submits that since previously there was no specific direction of the Ministry of Public Administration for allocation of marks for written and viva voce examination, hence, the Selection Committee had decided independently to fix respective marks for written and viva Voce examination as 80% and 20%. Later, however, change in the marking system was made observing, the general directives of the government as issued by the Ministry of Public Administration vide Memo dated 05.12.2011, for the directions made by the said Ministry is mandatory to all the government departments in general. He further submits that in the recruitment advertisement no mention was made with regard to distribution of marks between written and viva voce examination nor the candidates or any other quarter was supposed to know the distribution of marks between written and viva voce examination; it was solely an internal arrangement of the authority concern. Hence, he submits that it is obvious that some vested quarters were motivated with malafide intention to hinder the recruitment process and upon collecting confidential official documents of the appointing authority had filed this writ petition. He further goes to submit that in the recruitment advertisement there was one condition that the decision of the appointing authority would be final in relation to the matter of appointment “ নিয়োগ সংক্রান্ত নিয়োগকারী কর্তৃপক্ষের সিদ্ধান্তই চুড়ান্ত বলিয়া গন্য হইবে। As such, he submits that any change as per government's valid order in the process of appointment is final. He also goes to argue that the circular dated 05.12.2011 issued by the Ministry of Public Administration Was not directed specifically to the present recruitment process, rather it was a common administrative direction given to all the concerned government departments to be followed. In the instant case, the appointing authority, the Directorate of Food, has brought the changes in marks distributions as per the said general circular of the Ministry of Public Administration with bonafide intention with a view to complete the process of recruitment as per the terms and conditions as stipulated in the advertisement. He further submits that the news item published in the daily "Prothom Alo" on 04.09.2013 was based on hypothetical assumptions, the appointing authority and its office were not involved in such assumed bribery in any manner whatsoever. Besides, the authority concerned had formally sent a rejoinder against such news item which was published in the said newspaper on 05.10.2013. Accordingly, he goes to submit that the recruitment process has already been completed and that the result could not be finally published due to pendency of the instant Rule. Accordingly he submits that this Rule being devoid of any substance is liable to be discharged. 

 19. The process of selection is the most crucial and important part of the recruitment exercise and involves a number of functional stage like inviting applications, scrutiny of applications, rejection of defective applications or eliminations of ineligible candidates, conducting examinations, calling for interview or viva voce and preparation of list of successful candidates for appointment, as has been observed in the case of A.P. Public Service Commission, Hydrabad Vs. B Sharat Chandra J.T.1990 (2) Supreme Court 143:(1990) 2SCC669. However, in its true sense the process begins when the stage of evaluation of the merits of the candidates is reached. Generally, the task of selection is assigned to a selection committee. The functions of such committee is to those amongst the eligible candidates on the basis of merit adjudged by adopting fairly, laid down criteria and finally preparing a panel or select list of the successful or selected candidates, as has been categorically found in National Institution of Mental Health and Neuro Sciences Vs. Kalyana Raman 1992:Supp(2) SCC 481:AIR1992 Supreme Court 1806 where the Indian Supreme Court has further held that the function of a selection committee is neither judicial or adjudicatory, it is purely administrative. The Supreme Court, however, pointed out that the necessity for giving reasons of it's decision is different from, and in principle distinct from the requirements of procedural fairness. It reiterated that procedural fairness was the main requirement in administrative action and the selection committee was not an exception to this principle and must take a decision reasonably without being guided by extraneous or irrelevant considerations. In this regard, the selection committee must be properly constituted i.e., in accordance with the Rules or the administrative instruction which provides for such constitution. 

 28. The Directorate of Food pursuant to Memo No. প্রশা/সংস্থা/১ নিয়োগ-৯/২০১০-১১০৮ dated 16.09.2010 (Annexure-A) published a notification in the "Daily Star" on 21.09.2010(Annexure-B) for appointment of 1552 3rd Class posts in 10 different categories including 328 posts of Inspector of Food, 175 posts of Sub-Inspector of Food and 405 posts of Assistant Sub-Inspector of Food. However, for the posts of Food Inspector 1,21,157, for the post of Sub-Inspector of Food 16,308 and Assistant Sub-Inspector of Food 29,710 candidates applied. Their written examinations were duly held on 22.12.2011, 23.12.2011 and 25.05.2012 respectively. In the said examination 2939 against the post of Food Inspector, 2578 against the posts of Sub-Inspector of Food and 3686 against the post of Assistant Sub-Inspector of Food came eat successful (Annexure-4). 

 29. It, however, appears from Annexure-G, the minutes of the Selection Committee dated 22.07.2013 that earlier the Committee in it's meeting dated 05.12.2011 took decision to take written examination in 100 marks for the post of Food Inspector, Sub-Inspector of Food and Assistant Sub-Inspector of Food to be evaluated in 80% marks and viva voce examination to be held on the remaining 20% marks. Pursuant to the said decision written examinations were duly held on 23.12.2011 and 25.05.2012 respectively and the result was also published on 11.01.2012 and 11.10.2012 respectively. While the candidates were awaiting the date for viva voce examination all on a sudden the Selection Committee had changed the marking criteria in it's meeting dated 22.07.2013 for the 3rd and 4th  Class administrative posts, fixing 70% for the written and 30% for viva voce examination after about 1½  year later. In support the respondent-government contends that such change of marking criteria was made pursuant to Memo No.142 dated 05.05.2013 (Annexure-2) issued by the Ministry of Public Administrative, for the directions made by the said Ministry is mandatory to all government offices in general. The contents of the said Memo is quoted below- 

 33. However, from Annexure-4 it appears that publication of the result of the written examination of all the 8(eight) categories of posts were made within 07.10.2011-11.01.2012; however, for leak out of the question paper of the examinations for the posts of Assistant Sub-Inspector of Food and Office Assistant-cum Computer Typist were suspended for certain period of time. Ultimately, it was taken afresh on 25.05.2012 and the result was published on 11.10.2012. As such, the question remains if the viva voce examination of 6(six) other categories could be completed prior to issuance of instruction of the Ministry of Public Administration vide Memo dated 05.05.2013 why viva voce examination of 4(four) other categories could not be completed even in between 11.10.2012 and 05.05.2013 i.e., the last date of publication of result of the written examination of Assistant Sub-Inspector of Food and Office Assistant-cum Computer Operator and the date of issuance of the office order of the Ministry of Public Administration ( within the span of more than 6(six) months). In the said context sudden rush in completing the selection process i.e., holding viva voce examination by the Selection Committees of the Directorate of Food of 2939 candidates for the post of Inspector of Food in 7(seven) working days (Annexure-C), 2578 candidates for the posts of Sub-Inspector of Food in 6(six) working days(Annexure-D) and 3686 candidates for the posts of Assistant Sub-Inspector of Food in 9(nine) working days(Annexure-E), becomes questionable.
